# DSH Session Rail
A per-session right sidebar preview for DeepSeek Harness (DSH). It displays Environment, Context, Pl
ugins, and Git Changes in that order.
## Requirements

- DSH Web with the right-sidebar tab package available.
- Node.js `>=22.19.0` on the DSH Host.

The Environment card shows the Session's project folder name, full path, and current Git branch. Con
text reads DSH token-meter projections (`contextPressure`, `contextBreakdown`, `tokenUsage`) and, wh
en the optional `dsh-context` plugin is installed, the fine-grained `contextTimeline` projection. Th
e panel shows a colored category occupancy bar, per-category shares, expandable assistant detail whe
n present, timing/cache rows when the source provides them, and explicitly marks Claude-style catego
ries that DSH does not expose (MCP instructions, Memory, and Skills when only the coarse meter is av
ailable). Plugin names and enabled/runtime status come from DSH's public read-only plugin inventory.
Changes lists the Session workspace's changed files, staged/unstaged state, and line counts. `Commit
changes` sends the fixed user message `Commit the working tree changes with a sensible message.` to
that Session's live Agent. The Agent performs the commit through its normal tools; Session Rail nev
er stages, commits, pushes, or mutates files itself.
Selecting a changed file opens the page kind entered in the `Review page` field, such as `codex-revi
ew`. The field offers every active page tab published by the DSH `sidebarRightTabs` registry as a su
ggestion, while still allowing the kind to be entered directly. The choice is stored in browser `loc
alStorage`. If the selected page is unavailable, Session Rail shows an installation hint and falls b
ack to the bounded inline unified diff. Binaries show metadata without rendering contents.
The sidebar tab is available from the right-sidebar tab picker and from the small button in the Sess
ion header. Switching Sessions uses that Session's own workspace and context projections.
